said that new data from a phase 3 trial found that patients receiving a subcutaneous version of Skyrizi (risankizumab) for Crohn's disease had higher rates of endoscopic remission and ulcer-free endoscopy vs. placebo.
At week 24, endoscopic remission was seen in 35.8% of patients on Skyrizi, and 36.6% of patients who had ulcers at the start of the study achieved the complete absence of ulcers.
from the AFFIRM study found that in patients who had yet to receive advanced therapy, at week 24, 45.1% saw endoscopic remission and 49% achieved ulcer-free endoscopy.
In the trial, 65% of participants had previously failed on advanced therapies.
AbbVie noted that applications for subcutaneous induction therapy of Skyrizi are before the US FDA and the European Medicines Agency.

title: AbbVie releases phase 3 induction therapy data on injectable Skyrizi for Crohn's
